refutation.quote: Zeroing the down_proj columns of 1,000 MLP neurons (0.28 %) ranked on 14 real loops by attribution: loops 71 -> 19, cap hits 98 -> 39, tokens/problem 3,870 (-17 %), right 381 (+0.6 points [-3.4, 4.6]).
refutation.note: This is squarely in scope: cued Olmo-3 base, MATH-500, T 0.6, cap hits. At T 0.6 the base's loops fall from 71 to 19 when a specific set of loop-driving neurons is removed (1,000 random neurons do nothing: 74 loops). No tail mass is restored and no hold-on tokens are added. So under sharpening, loop lock-in is carried by a specific neuron circuit that can be cut directly; 'the escape mass was deleted' is not the only route. Removing about 60 cap hits also adds only +0.6 points, while T 1.0 versus T 0.6 is about 32 points (410 vs 378). That undercuts the theory's implied claim that the loop component carries a meaningful share of the temperature effect, and with it P2 (theta0.25 at T 0.6 scoring 437). It does not refute the mechanism outright: the theory never says loops cannot be cut another way. Other things I read: (a) arXiv 2610.30882 (via recall), Sec 4 / Table 14: 'at temperature 0.6 ... 29.1% of its responses reach the length limit (base 17.8%)' for Olmo-3-7B-RL-Zero-Math. That directly contradicts 'RL is insensitive to temperature', but it uses the 3.0 release and an 8,192 cap, while the theory's scope is 3.1 at 16,384, and result-533123 (3.1, -0.2 points [-1.8, 1.4]) supports the theory. (b) result-c4411d: RL-base +0.066 [0.061, 0.072]. That interval excludes 0, so the push is not strictly context-free, but the effect is small. (c) result-36e8cd: late-MLP RL directions read Okay/consider/Wait, which supports the theory. (d) result-afc423, result-44b4df, knowledge-1497e8. None of the held-out items or new board items tests the core predictions: constant vectors at T 0.6 (P1), theta0.25 at T 0.6 (P2), or how the hold-on rate depends on temperature (P3-P5; all three offline tests are 'not computed' because S3 returned 403).

wins_judgement: There is one scored claim, t13 (+0.667 nats): RL-minus-base rise in hold-on log-prob after a wrong result, predicted 0 [-0.25, 0.25], measured 0.066. The win comes from 'a constant, context-free push', which was already on the board before the cutoff (result-cb82cf 'general habit, not error-specific'; result-54f212 constant per-layer vectors). The tail-escape and temperature mechanism plays no part in it. The reversal, which states the opposite direction of hold-on change, made the same 'constant shift gives about 0' argument, predicted 0.05 and gained +0.289. The gap over the reversal (+0.38) is the advocate's narrower interval, not the mechanism. A reader holding cb82cf would have made this claim. The nulls (0.15 and 0.2, with wider intervals) lost only because they were vaguer. The total is one target with a degenerate interval [0.667, 0.667], so the evidence for the mechanism is essentially nil.
rival: The rival (low-entropy collapse from weak continuation of the model's own long context, knowledge-1497e8; RL fixes content) makes no specific prediction for t13. If anything, a content-fixing RL predicts error-specific reading, and c4411d's small +0.066 together with chains -0.007 (t14) lean slightly against it. So t13 does not separate the two. The targets that would separate them are not held out: P1 (cap hits at T 0.6 with the 32 constant vectors added; rival about 119, theory 30-75) and P3/P4 (the base's hold-on rate rising with T while RL's stays flat). result-6de887 (loops cut by neuron ablation with no accuracy gain) fits the rival at least as well as the theory: a removed loop becomes a fresh draw at a problem the base still cannot solve.

novelty.nearest: Chen & Wang 2026, 'When Do Repetition Loops Lock?': under top-p/min-p, a loop position becomes deterministic (escape probability exactly 0) once the loop token's probability crosses the truncation threshold. Pure sampling never locks, and temperature before truncation lowers the lock threshold (Theorem 1, Prop. 3). Lee et al. 2026 (cited there) relate loop persistence to the escape mass the sampling set leaves. The process-word push is from 2509.06608 (RL steering vectors in Qwen2.5-Math promote process words over 'solution').
novelty.difference: The paper proves that truncation and low temperature remove the escape mass and lock loops. It does not say that RL moves the escape into high-probability process tokens through a constant per-layer push, making RL and small doses of its delta temperature-robust.

import_carries_gain.which: The import (2509.06608: RL steering vectors promote process words) supports the 'constant push toward Wait/Hmm' half, and t13 rests on 'constant push'. But the same argument was available from in-house result-54f212 and result-cb82cf, and the reversal reached nearly the same number with the opposite token direction. The paper's specific finding (a penultimate-layer vector promoting process words to deter premature endings) does not set the value 0 or its interval for t13. The import's distinctive consequence is P1 (constant vectors make the base robust to sharpening), and that is untested.

verdict: weak: its single winning claim (t13, +0.67 nats) comes from the 'constant push' reading that was already on the board and that the reversal shared, not from the tail-escape mechanism. The loop-locking half is published (2610.24715), the core predictions (P1, P2 and the offline hold-on ratios) are untested, and result-6de887 shows T 0.6 loops can be cut by neuron ablation with no accuracy gain.
